name: node_group
description: Manages a DuploCloud AI Helpdesk AWS EKS managed node group.

attributes.name: workspace_id
attributes.description: ID of the workspace that owns this node group.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: Name of the node group.

attributes.name: description
attributes.description: Optional description.

attributes.name: scope_ids
attributes.description: Scope IDs that link this node group to a cloud provider account.

attributes.name: resource_group_id
attributes.description: ID of the resource group (EKS cluster, under an environment) this node group belongs to.

attributes.name: environment_id
attributes.description: ID of the environment that owns the resource group.

attributes.name: instance_types
attributes.description: EC2 instance types for the node group (e.g. t3.medium).

attributes.name: min_size
attributes.description: Minimum number of nodes.

attributes.name: max_size
attributes.description: Maximum number of nodes.

attributes.name: desired_size
attributes.description: Desired number of nodes (between min_size and max_size).

attributes.name: enable_cluster_autoscaler
attributes.description: Tag this node group's Auto Scaling group for discovery by the Kubernetes Cluster Autoscaler. The cluster_autoscaler component must also be enabled on the cluster via duploai_cluster_attributes for autoscaling to take effect.

attributes.name: disk_size_gb
attributes.description: Root EBS volume size in GiB for each node.

attributes.name: kms_key_id
attributes.description: KMS key ARN or ID used to encrypt the node group's EBS volumes. Leave unset to use the AWS-managed default key. Immutable after creation.

attributes.name: volumes
attributes.description: Additional EBS volumes attached to every node, beyond the root volume sized by disk_size_gb. Maximum 4 entries; device_name must be unique per entry and cannot be /dev/xvda (the root device). Per-volume KMS encryption is not supported here — disk encryption is controlled by the node group's own kms_key_id/encryption settings.

attributes.name: device_name
attributes.description: Device name as it appears on the instance (e.g. /dev/xvdb).

attributes.name: volume_size_gb
attributes.description: Volume size in GiB.

attributes.name: volume_type
attributes.description: EBS volume type: gp2, gp3, io1, io2, st1, or sc1. Defaults to gp3.

attributes.name: iops
attributes.description: Provisioned IOPS. Only valid for gp3, io1, and io2 volume types.

attributes.name: throughput
attributes.description: Provisioned throughput in MiB/s. Only valid for gp3 volumes.

attributes.name: delete_on_termination
attributes.description: Whether the volume is deleted when the node is terminated.

attributes.name: encrypted
attributes.description: Whether the volume is encrypted at rest.

attributes.name: snapshot_id
attributes.description: Snapshot ID to restore the volume from.

attributes.name: capacity_type
attributes.description: EC2 purchasing model for the nodes: ON_DEMAND (the server default) for standard pricing, or SPOT for cheaper capacity that AWS can reclaim at any time. Immutable after creation.

attributes.name: ami_type
attributes.description: EKS-optimised AMI the nodes boot from. Leave it unset in most cases: the platform then resolves a type that suits both the cluster's Kubernetes version and the instance types' architecture, and records the value it chose. Setting it explicitly overrides that resolution, and the API validates the value against the types it currently supports — so a value this description does not list may still be accepted, and an unsupported one is rejected by the API rather than by AWS minutes into the CloudFormation stack. At the time of writing: the AL2_* types (AL2_x86_64, AL2_x86_64_GPU, AL2_ARM_64) are Amazon Linux 2 and are accepted only through Kubernetes 1.32, while the AL2023_* types (AL2023_x86_64_STANDARD, AL2023_x86_64_NVIDIA, AL2023_ARM_64_STANDARD) are Amazon Linux 2023 and are required from 1.33 onward. Match the variant to the instance types — ARM_64 for Graviton families (those ending in g, such as m7g), the GPU/NVIDIA variants for GPU workloads — since no single AMI boots both architectures. To boot your own image instead, set ami_type = "CUSTOM" and image_id to the AMI's id: CUSTOM is the only value that accepts image_id, and it requires it, while every other value rejects it. A custom AMI must derive from an EKS-optimised AL2023 image so that nodeadm is present, because the launch template pins your image and injects nodeadm bootstrap user data — EKS does not supply bootstrap config for custom AMIs, and an image without nodeadm provisions successfully and then never joins the cluster. The platform preflights the id's existence and architecture in the cluster's region, so a wrong-architecture or cross-region id fails early rather than as a late stack rollback. Immutable after creation.

attributes.name: image_id
attributes.description: AMI ID for the nodes, e.g. ami-0c02fb55956c7d316. Required when ami_type is CUSTOM and rejected for every other ami_type. The AMI must derive from an EKS-optimised AL2023 image so nodeadm is present: the launch template pins the image and injects nodeadm bootstrap user data, because EKS stops supplying bootstrap config for custom AMIs — an AMI without it provisions successfully and then never joins the cluster. The platform preflights the id's existence and architecture in-region, so a wrong-architecture or cross-region id fails early. Immutable after creation.

attributes.name: additional_labels
attributes.description: Kubernetes labels applied to the nodes.

attributes.name: taints
attributes.description: Kubernetes taints applied to the nodes.

attributes.name: key
attributes.description: Taint key.

attributes.name: value
attributes.description: Taint value.

attributes.name: effect
attributes.description: Taint effect. Accepted values are defined by the backend EksNodeGroupTaintEffect enum (e.g. NoSchedule/PreferNoSchedule/NoExecute); confirm the exact value against your tenant.

attributes.name: tags
attributes.description: AWS tags applied to the node group, its Auto Scaling Group, and its EC2 instances/EBS volumes. Keys cannot use the reserved prefixes duplocloud.ai/ or k8s.io/cluster-autoscaler/, or the reserved names resourcegroup, environment, allocationtags, or duplo-resource-id (use enable_cluster_autoscaler instead of setting a cluster-autoscaler tag directly). Subject to AWS limits: max 50 tags, keys up to 128 characters, values up to 256 characters.

attributes.name: allocation_tag
attributes.description: Allocation tag used to target workloads to this node group.

attributes.name: instance_visibility
attributes.description: Node placement visibility: Internal places nodes in private subnets only (the default, and the platform's own default), Public places them in public subnets only. Immutable after creation.

attributes.name: provisioner_type
attributes.description: Provisioner type: Cli, IacNativeTf, IacDuploTf, or DirectApiCall.

attributes.name: provisioner_version
attributes.description: Optional provisioner version.

attributes.name: status
attributes.description: Current provisioning status.

attributes.name: node_group_id
attributes.description: ID of this node group, for reference by dependent resources.

attributes.name: node_group_name
attributes.description: Provisioned EKS node group name.

attributes.name: node_group_arn
attributes.description: ARN of the provisioned node group.

attributes.name: stack_id
attributes.description: ID of the underlying provisioning stack.

attributes.name: kubernetes_version
attributes.description: Kubernetes version of the node group.

attributes.name: release_version
attributes.description: AMI release version of the node group.

attributes.name: asg_name
attributes.description: Name of the backing Auto Scaling group.

attributes.name: live_cluster_autoscaler_enabled
attributes.description: Whether the cluster autoscaler currently recognizes and manages this node group's Auto Scaling group, as observed live from AWS.

attributes.name: subnet_ids
attributes.description: Subnets the node group is deployed into.

invalidWhen.message: image_id may only be set when ami_type is "CUSTOM" — every other ami_type selects an AWS-managed EKS AMI and the API rejects an explicit image id alongside it.
